title: Merkle allowlist (prove you are on the list)
blurb: The owner publishes one 32-byte root for a list of thousands of accounts. A member proves membership with a handful of hashes instead of the whole list. Succinct proofs are what ZK is made of; this is the hash-only version.
steps: Build, Test, Ship (any root is fine for init).
Use the MERKLE helper under BUILD (or m near/merkle alice.testnet,bob.testnet,you.testnet) to get a root and each account's proof.
CHANGE claim {"proof":[...]} from a listed account; VIEW claimed and claims.
Try claim from an account that is not on the list: refused with the same few hashes.

walkthrough.say: Each account becomes a leaf: sha256 of its name. Hashing the leaf (not using the raw name) means a proof element can never be mistaken for a leaf.
Pairs are sorted before hashing, so a proof does not need left/right flags: whichever order the two hashes come in, the parent is the same.
Walk from the leaf to the top: hash with each proof element in turn. If you land on the root, you are on the list. The list itself never touches the chain; just one root.
Changing the list = changing 32 bytes. Airdrops and allowlists do exactly this for hundreds of thousands of addresses.

Membership plus one-time-ness: the contract remembers who claimed. A ZK version would replace the account id with a nullifier so even WHO claimed stays hidden; see the zuma and zquorum mods for that, in Cairo.
